text: How much of your workday is repetitive – the same steps, templates, similar documents or requests?
help: The more repetitive information work there is, the easier it is to automate.

text: How much of your work is direct contact with people (clients, patients, students, your team)?
help: Trust, empathy and negotiation are the hardest things for AI.

options.label: A large part of the day
It is the core of my job

text: Does your work require being physically present or working with your hands?
help: Robotics is advancing much more slowly than language models.

options.label: No, I work at a computer
Most of my work is physical

text: How often do you make decisions in unclear situations and take responsibility for the outcome?
help: Accountability cannot be delegated to AI (yet).

text: How much experience do you have in your field?
help: Entry-level tasks get automated first – experience brings context and judgment.

text: Do you have knowledge that cannot be found online (internal processes, client relationships, local regulation, a special niche)?
help: Unique context is what AI does not know – and what you can amplify with AI.

text: How often do you use AI tools (ChatGPT, Claude, Copilot, Gemini or similar) in your work?
help: A person who uses AI is the most likely to replace one who does not.

text: What best describes your AI skills?
help: Pick the highest level that fits you.

options.label: I don't know where to start
I give context, examples and a format – and get consistently good results
I have built automations, agents or solutions on an AI API

text: How quickly do you adopt a new tool or way of working?
help: AI tools change in months, not years.

options.label: I tend to wait until others have tried it
I learn it when I need to
I try new things myself, quickly

text: Do your employer or clients already use AI in their work processes?
help: When an organization is already moving, roles change faster – that is both a risk and an opportunity.

text: How many hours a week can you realistically spend on learning?
help: We use this to estimate how long the learning path will take.
